extracted.intended_audience: publishers, repositories, aggregators, libraries, researchers, editors, indexers, journalists, and readers (scholarly-publishing stakeholders)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for how to represent, transfer, and display the editorial status (retractions, removals, expressions of concern) of published scholarly works so that humans and machines can readily detect and act on those statuses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential data elements for retractions/removals/EOCs
rubrics_metrics.description: The recommended practice describes the essential data elements required to effectively communicate retractions, removals and expressions of concern (EOCs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CREC recommended practice 'describes the essential data elements required to effectively communicate retractions, removals and EOCs.' These elements are intended to be used so post-publication editorial action is easily identified by both human and machine readers across publisher platforms and aggregators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metadata transfer (machine-readable exchange)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on the transfer of required metadata elements between publishers, aggregators, repositories, and other services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CREC includes 'guidance on the required meta-data elements, their transfer, and display.' The practice identifies responsibilities for each step of correct dissemination so metadata propagates reliably across systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display of editorial status to human readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for how the retracted/removed/EOC status should be displayed to readers on publisher platforms and aggregators so the updated editorial status is imminently clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations are intended to ensure information regarding retractions, removals, and EOCs 'are disseminated effectively, transparently, and rapidly, so that the updated editorial status of the work is imminently clear.' Emphasis on visibility for human readers and avoidance of inconsistent display across resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine-actionable signalling of editorial changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure post-publication editorial actions are identifiable by machines (indexers, citation databases, discovery systems) as well as humans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CREC 'presents a number of items that ensure post-publication editorial action is easily identified by both human and machine readers.' This covers use of consistent metadata fields and transfer protocols to allow automated systems to flag or suppress retracted content appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear assignment of responsibilities/roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the parties involved in and responsible for communicating editorial decisions and for each step of metadata dissemination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidelines 'identify the parties responsible for each step of the correct dissemination of the information regarding the updated editorial status of the affected article.' This is intended to remove ambiguity about who must update metadata, notify aggregators, or amend platform displays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness / rapid dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial-status updates should be disseminated rapidly so that subsequent users encounter the corrected status as soon as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CREC stresses dissemination that is 'effective, transparently, and rapidly' to combat continued inappropriate citations of retracted articles; speed of metadata propagation is presented as a core desideratum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications about retractions/removals/EOCs should be transparent—making clear what happened and the current status without obscuration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recommended practice aims for information to be 'disseminated effectively, transparently' so readers and systems understand the editorial action and its basis (while noting CREC does not advise on whether to issue decisions themselves). Transparency also helps trust in research and scholarship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope-limitation: not advising editorial decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: The CREC guidelines do not provide guidance on whether or how editors should issue retractions/removals/EOCs; their scope is dissemination rather than editorial judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly: 'the CREC guidelines do not advise editors on issuing editorial decisions, rather these guidelines are intended to ensure information regarding retractions, removals, and EOCs are disseminated effectively.' This delimits the recommended practice's remit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling complex/large-scale or manipulation-linked retractions
rubrics_metrics.description: Special guidance for complicated situations such as simultaneous, large-scale retraction cases linked to manipulation of the publication process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CREC 'discuss more complicated situations, such as simultaneous, large-scale retraction cases linked to manipulation of the publication process,' providing recommendations relevant to mass or coordinated issues where standard workflows may be insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for actions on pre-versions of record and related objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations for how to communicate editorial actions that affect pre-versions of record (preprints, accepted manuscripts) and related versions of an item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The practice covers 'editorial action taken on the pre-versions of record,' indicating that metadata and display rules should account for multiple versions and ensure all affected manifestations are correctly flagged and linked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination following change of publisher or platform
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for how retraction/removal/EOC information should be shared and preserved when content changes publisher or platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CREC provides 'guidance for the dissemination of retractions, removals, and EOCs following change of publishers,' to prevent loss of status information during transfers and ensure continued visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations for non-English materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice for sharing retraction/removal/EOC information for materials published in languages other than English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidelines include 'recommendations for the sharing of this information involving materials published in languages other than English,' acknowledging multilingual publication ecosystems and the need for inclusive dissemination practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal: reduce inappropriate citation of retracted work
rubrics_metrics.description: Aims and metrics to combat the continued propagation of retracted work being cited as if not retracted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motivated by research showing only 5–20% of citations acknowledge retraction, CREC's visibility and metadata recommendations are framed to reduce cases where retracted publications 'continue to be cited as if the retraction had not occurred.' This is an intended outcome and evaluative goal for effective implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocacy for community adoption and awareness-raising
rubrics_metrics.description: Call for publishers, repositories, indexers, researchers, journalists, and readers to share and adopt the CREC recommended practice to ensure its effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The working group 'encourage publishers, repositories, abstracting and indexing providers, researchers, journalists, and readers to share the CREC guidelines with their respective networks to increase awareness and encourage their adoption into the wider industry.' Adoption and community outreach are treated as necessary for success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance: standing committee to monitor and update CREC
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a CREC standing committee to monitor changes in the industry and issue updates to the recommended practice when relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post notes formation of a standing committee because 'the publishing industry will change over time' and some topics (e.g., taxonomy, suppression of HTML) were unresolved; ongoing governance is recommended to keep the practice current.
